{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '<file name="D:\\dev\\ab-tasks\\_briefs\\raptor\\brief.md">\n# Task Brief: Port Raptor: Call of the Shadows (Sector 1) to HTML5\n\n## 1. Goal\n\nPort *Raptor: Call of the Shadows* (Apogee, 1994) — sector 1 only, the shareware\ncontent — from the original DOS game to a browser game built with HTML5 canvas,\nvanilla JavaScript, and the Web Audio API. The port must render real game assets\n(graphics and sounds) extracted from the original shareware data files, either at\nbuild time or at runtime — no placeholder art, no placeholder audio. Do not use\nany external frameworks or libraries beyond what ships in the browser (no React,\nPhaser, PixiJS, Howler, etc.). A small vanilla test runner is fine if you want\none, but it is not required.\n\n## 2. Worktree Layout\n\nYour worktree root (`./`) contains the GPL C/ASM source of the original DOS game,\nprovided for reference and porting purposes, under `SOURCE/`, `GFX/`, `audiolib/`,\nand `apodmx/`. It also contains the original shareware game data files under\n`./data/` — GLB archive files, the shareware `RAP.EXE` for reference, and whatever\nelse the shareware distribution contained.\n\nBuild your web port as new files alongside/above this existing tree (for example\n`index.html`, an asset-extraction or build script, and your JS source), and keep\nthe original source tree intact for reference — do not delete or rewrite it.\n\nYou must write and maintain a `README` documenting a working dev-server command\n(for example `npx serve .`, `python -m http.server`, or similar) so that the port\ncan be opened and played in a browser at any milestone. Keep this command accurate\nand working as you go — it will be used to check your progress at each milestone.\n\n## 3. Standing Rules\n\n- Vanilla JavaScript + HTML5 canvas + Web Audio API only. No external runtime\n  frameworks or libraries. A lightweight bundler or dev-only tool is fine if it\n  produces plain output, but avoid dependency-heavy tooling.\n- Always leave behind a documented, working dev server command that serves a\n  working build.\n- Commit to git after completing each milestone (M1 through M5, below), so\n  progress is checkpointed.\n- Sector 1 (shareware) content only — you do not need to support later sectors\n  or the registered/full game.\n\n## 4. Milestone Ladder (M1–M5)\n\nThis is the actual grading spec. Copied verbatim:\n\n- **M1**: level-1 background + player ship rendered on canvas from the real GLB\n  data. Graded by screenshot similarity (SSIM) to a reference DOSBox frame on the\n  playfield region (target >= 0.80), and >= 90% of the reference color palette\n  present.\n- **M2**: arrow keys move the ship; firing spawns a projectile.\n- **M3**: wave-1 enemies spawn; a projectile hit decrements enemy HP or removes\n  the enemy; the player can die.\n- **M4**: HUD (score/shields) renders; a Web Audio context is running and at\n  least one sound effect is triggered on firing.\n- **M5**: the sector-1 loop completes — the wave counter advances through wave 9\n  and a sector-complete screen appears.\n\n## 5. Grader Interface Contract\n\nYou **must** implement exactly this. An automated Playwright script checks\nagainst it — this is a hard requirement, not a suggestion.\n\n- A canvas element `<canvas id="raptor-canvas">` whose internal pixel buffer is\n  exactly 320x200 (`canvas.width === 320`, `canvas.height === 200`), independent\n  of any CSS display scaling.\n- Controls: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` / `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` move the ship;\n  the Space bar fires. Use standard `keydown`/`keyup` DOM listeners — no custom\n  input hook needed.\n- A live-updated global object `window.__raptor` with this exact shape:\n\n  ```js\n  window.__raptor = {\n    ready: boolean,            // true once the first frame (background + player ship) is drawn from real game data\n    player: { x: number, y: number, alive: boolean },\n    projectiles: [ { x: number, y: number, owner: \'player\'|\'enemy\' }, /* ... */ ],\n    enemies: [ { id: string|number, hp: number, x: number, y: number, alive: boolean }, /* ... */ ],\n    hud: { score: number, shields: number },\n    audio: { contextState: \'running\'|\'suspended\'|\'closed\', sfxCount: number },  // sfxCount increments on every SFX triggered\n    wave: number,               // current wave within sector 1\n    sectorComplete: boolean\n  };\n  ```\n\n- Keep this object\'s fields in sync with actual game state at all times. The\n  grader polls it, drives real keyboard input to test M2/M3/M4/M5, and takes a\n  canvas screenshot to test M1. For M5 the grader is allowed to auto-play (hold\n  fire, jitter movement) rather than requiring skilled play, so you do not need\n  to build any special "autoplay" or "god mode" feature — just make the interface\n  accurately reflect real game state during ordinary play.\n\n</file>\n'}], 'attribution': 'user', 'timestamp': 1787268741518}

key[ kidx ] - prev_byte ) % 256;\n      prev_byte = *buffer;\n      *buffer++ = dchr;\n  \n      if ( ++kidx >= klen )\n         kidx = 0;\n   }\n}\n\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\n   GLB_FindFile() - Opens & Caches file handle\n ------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\nPRIVATE INT\nGLB_OpenFile(\nINT\treturn_on_failure,\t// INPUT : Don\'t bomb if file not open\nINT\tfilenum,             // INPUT : file number\nINT\tpermissions\t\t\t\t// INPUT : file access permissions\n)\n{\n   FILEDESC    *fd;\n\n   ASSERT( filenum >= 0 && filenum < MAX_GLB_FILES );\n\n   fd = &filedesc[ filenum ];\n\n   if ( fd->handle == 0 )\n      return GLB_FindFile( return_on_failure, filenum, permissions );\n   else if ( fd->permissions != permissions )\n   {\n      close( fd->handle );\n   \tif ( ( fd->handle = open( fd->filepath, permissions ) ) == -1 )\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tif ( return_on_failure )\n\t\t\t\treturn -1;\n\n   \t   EXIT_Error ("GLB_OpenFile: %s, Error #%d,%s",\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\tfd->filepath, errno, strerror( errno ) );\n      }\n   }\n   else\n   {\n      lseek( fd->handle, 0L, SEEK_SET );\n   }\n   return fd->handle;\n}\n  \n\n/*------------------------------------------------------------------------\n   GLB_CloseFiles() - {'role': 'toolResult', 'toolCallId': 'chatcmpl-tool-81eb4f9439738d38', 'toolName': 'read', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n  \n#include "raptor.h"\n  \n#define MAX_STILES ( MAP_ONSCREEN * MAP_COLS )\n  \nPUBLIC DWORD   titems [ MAP_SIZE ];\nPUBLIC DWORD   eitems [ MAP_SIZE ];\nPUBLIC SHORT   hits [ MAP_SIZE ];\nPUBLIC SHORT   money [ MAP_SIZE ];\nPUBLIC SHORT   tdead [ MAP_SIZE ];\nPUBLIC DWORD   startflat[4];\nPUBLIC INT     tilepos;\nPUBLIC INT     tileyoff;\n  \nPUBLIC INT     g_mapleft;\nPUBLIC BYTE *  tilepic;\nPUBLIC BYTE *  tilestart;\nPUBLIC INT     tileloopy;\n  \nPRIVATE CHAR game_start [4][17] = {\n   "STARTG1TILES",\n   "STARTG2TILES",\n   "STARTG3TILES",\n   "STARTG4TILES"\n};\n  \nPUBLIC BOOL          scroll_flag;\nPUBLIC BOOL          last_tile;\n\nPRIVATE TILESPOT     tspots [ MAX_STILES ];\nPRIVATE TILESPOT *   lastspot;\n\nPUBLIC TILEDELAY    first_delay;\nPUBLIC TILEDELAY    last_delay;\nPUBLIC TILEDELAY *  free_delay;\n\n#define MAX_TILEDELAY ( ( MAP_ONSCREEN + 1 ) * MAP_COLS )\nPRIVATE TILEDELAY tdel [ MAX_TILEDELAY ];\n\nPRIVATE INT spark_delay = 0;\nPRIVATE INT flare_delay = 0;\n\n/*-------------------------------------------------------------------------*\nTClear () - Clears TILE Delay Link List\n *-------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\nPRIVATE VOID\nTClear (\nVOID\n)\n{\n   INT loop;\n  \n   first_delay.prev = NUL;\n   first_delay.next = &last_delay;\n  \n   last_delay.prev = &first_delay;\n   last_delay.next = NUL;\n  \n   free_delay = tdel;\n  \n   memset ( tdel, 0, sizeof ( tdel ) );\n  \n   for ( loop = 0; loop < MAX_TILEDELAY-1; loop++ )\n      tdel[ loop ].next = &tdel [ loop + 1 ];\n}\n  \n/*-------------------------------------------------------------------------*\nTGet () - Get a TDELAY object\n *-------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\nPRIVATE TILEDELAY *\nTGet (\nVOID\n)\n{\n   TILEDELAY * new;\n  \n   if ( !free_delay )\n      EXIT_Error ("TILEDELAY_Get() - Max ");\n  \n   new = free_delay;\n   free_delay = free_delay->next;\n  \n   memset ( new, 0 ,sizeof ( TILEDELAY ) );\n  \n   new->next = &last_delay;\n   new->prev = last_delay.prev;\n   last_delay.prev = new;\n   new->prev->next = new;\n  \n   return ( new );\n}\n  \n/*-------------------------------------------------------------------------*\nTRemove () - Remove a TDELAY Object from link list\n *-------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\nPRIVATE TILEDELAY *\nTRemove (\nTILEDELAY * sh\n)\n{\n   TILEDELAY * next;\n  \n   next = sh->prev;\n  \n   sh->next->prev = sh->prev;\n   sh->prev->next = sh->next;\n  \n   memset ( sh, 0, sizeof ( TILEDELAY ) );\n  \n   sh->next = free_delay;\n  \n   free_delay = sh;\n  \n   return ( next );\n}\n\n/*--------------------------------------------------------------------------\nTILE_DoDamage\n --------------------------------------------------------------------------*/\nPRIVATE VOID\nTILE_DoDamage (\nINT   mapspot,\nINT   damage\n)\n{\n   static INT mlookup [3]  = { -1, -MAP_COLS, 1 };\n   static INT xlookup [3]  = { -1, 0, 1 };\n   INT ix                  = ( mapspot % MAP_COLS );\n   INT loop;\n   INT spot;\n   INT x;\n\n   for ( loop = 0; loop < 3; loop++ )\n   {\n      spot = mapspot + mlookup [ loop ];\n\n      if ( spot < 0 ) continue;\n      if ( spot >= MAP_SIZE ) continue;\n\n      if ( eitems [ spot ] == titems [ spot ] ) continue;\n\n      x = ix + xlookup [ loop ];\n      if ( x < 0 ) continue;\n      if ( x >= MAP_COLS ) continue;\n      \n      hits [ spot ] -= damage;\n   }\n\n}\n\n/***************************************************************************\nTILE_Draw () - Draws 32 by 32 TILE Clips on y only\n ***************************************************************************/\nVOID\nTILE_Put (\nBYTE * inpic,              // INPUT : pointer to GFX_PIC ( norm )\nINT    x,                  // INPUT : x position\nINT    y                   // INPUT : y position\n)\n{\n   BOOL flag = FALSE;\n  \n   if ( y + 32 <= 0 ) return;\n   if ( y >= SCREENHEIGHT ) return;\n  \n   tileloopy   = 32;\n   tilepic     = inpic;\n  \n   if ( y < 0 )\n   {\n      tilepic += FMUL32 ( -y );\n      tileloopy += y;\n      y = 0;\n      flag = TRUE;\n   }\n  \n   if ( y + tileloopy > SCREENHEIGHT )\n   {\n      tileloopy = SCREENHEIGHT - y;\n      flag = TRUE;\n   }\n  \n   tilestart = displaybuffer + x + ylookup [ y ];\n  \n   if ( flag )\n      TILE_ClipDraw();\n   else\n      TILE_Draw();\n}\n  \n/***************************************************************************\nTILE_Init () - Sets Up A level for Displaying\n ***************************************************************************/\nVOID\nTILE_Init (\nVOID\n)\n{\n  \n   TClear();\n   g_mapleft = MAP_LEFT;\n\n   scroll_flag = TRUE;\n   last_tile = FALSE;\n\n   // FIND START OF GAME TILES ========\n   startflat[0] = GLB_GetItemID ( game_start[ 0 ] );\n   startflat[0]++;\n  \n   startflat[1] = GLB_GetItemID ( game_start[ 1 ] );\n   startflat[1]++;\n  \n   startflat[2] = GLB_GetItemID ( game_start[ 2 ] );\n   startflat[2]++;\n  \n   startflat[3] = GLB_GetItemID ( game_start[ 3 ] );\n   startflat[3]++;\n\n}\n\n/***************************************************************************\nTILE_CacheLevel () - Cache tiles in current level\n ***************************************************************************/\nVOID\nTILE_CacheLevel (\nVOID\n)\n{\n   INT      game;\n   FLATS *  lib;\n   DWORD    item;\n   INT      loop;\n\n   TClear();\n   g_mapleft = MAP_LEFT;\n\n   // SET UP START POS ON MAP =========\n   tilepos = ( MAP_ROWS - MAP_ONSCREEN ) * MAP_COLS;\n   tileyoff = 200 - ( MAP_ONSCREEN * MAP_BLOCKSIZE );\n   lastspot = tspots + ( MAX_STILES - 1 );\n\n   scroll_flag = TRUE;\n   last_tile = FALSE;\n\n   memset ( titems, 0, sizeof (  titems ) );\n   memset ( eitems, 0, sizeof ( eitems ) );\n   memset ( hits, 0, sizeof ( hits ) );\n   memset ( tdead, 0, sizeof ( tdead ) );\n\n   // == CACHE TILES =========================\n   for ( loop = 0; loop < MAP_SIZE; loop++ )\n   {\n      game = ml->map [ loop ].fgame;\n      lib  = flatlib [ game ];\n\n      money [ loop ]  = lib [ ml->map [ loop ].flats ].bounty;\n\n      item = startflat [ game ];\n      item += ml->map [ loop ].flats;\n      titems [ loop ] = item;\n      GLB_CacheItem ( item );\n\n      item = startflat [ game ];\n      item += (DWORD)lib [ ml->map [ loop ].flats ].linkflat;\n      eitems [ loop ] = item;\n      if ( eitems [ loop ] !=  titems [ loop ] )\n         GLB_CacheItem ( item );\n\n      if ( eitems [ loop ] !=  titems [ loop ] )\n         hits [ loop ]  = lib [ ml->map [ loop ].flats ].bonus;\n      else\n         hits [ loop ]  = 1;\n   }\n}\n\n/***************************************************************************\nTILE_FreeLevel () - {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'The enemy spawn is tied to map scrolling. `tiley = (tilepos / MAP_COLS) - 3`, and spawns when `cur_enemy->y == tiley`. At frame 0, tilepos = 1278, tiley = 142 - 3 = 139. So enemies with y=139 would spawn at frame 0. The first CSPRITEs in the map might have y=139 or lower... At frame 0, tilepos=1278, tiley=139. If the first sprite has y=139, it spawns immediately. We\'ll need to see the map data.\n\nThis is getting complex. Let me now take a step back and think about the architecture and the practical approach.\n\n## Architecture Plan\n\nI\'ll build:\n1. **`tools/extract.mjs`** — Node.js build script that reads the GLB files, decrypts them, decodes all needed items, and writes a JSON bundle `assets/assets.json` containing:\n   - The full palette (PALETTE_DAT — 768 bytes → array of RGB)\n   - Images as indexed pixel data (width, height, palette indices) for all needed PICs/sprites/tiles\n   - The maps (MAZELEVEL)\n   - Sprite libraries (SPRITE array)\n   - Sound effects (as PCM arrays)\n   - Fonts (for HUD text)\n\n2. **`index.html`** — the game entry with `<canvas id="raptor-canvas" width="320" height="200">`.\n\n3. **`js/`** — the game source:\n   - `glb.js` — GLB decoder (used at runtime if we want, or just a bundle loader)\n   - `assets.js` — loads the bundle\n   - `gfx.js` — indexed graphics rendering to a 320×200 buffer, then blit to canvas (with CSS scaling)\n   - `game.js` — main game loop, state, waves\n   - `player.js`, `weapons.js`, `enemies.js`, `shots.js`, `eshot.js`, `tiles.js`, `audio.js`, `hud.js`, `input.js`\n\nActually, to keep it manageable and cohesive, I might do fewer files. But modular is better for maintainability. Let me aim for a clean set.\n\nFor rendering: the original game renders to a 320×200 byte buffer (displaybuffer, indexed), then blits to screen with palette. I\'ll replicate: keep an `ImageData`-like Uint8Array 320×200 of palette indices, render sprites via blitting (like GFX_PutSprite which uses transparency via a key color), then at display time map through palette → RGBA → putImageData on canvas. This is faithful and fast.\n\nKey detail — GFX_PutSprite transparency. Terminated when `offset == EMPTY` (0xFFFFFFFF). The offset is the offset within the image, x/y is the segment's position, length is the run length. Wait, let me reconsider. The `offset` field is a terminator sentinel (EMPTY=0xFFFFFFFF). Actually offset might be used for something but in the draw it's just a terminator check. So to decode: read GFX_SPRITE {x, y, offset, length}; if offset != 0xFFFFFFFF, then read `length` bytes of pixel data and place at (x+destx, y+desty).\n\n- `GPIC` (type=1): raw `width*height` bytes of indexed pixels.\n\nNow what about transparency in sprites? For GSPRITE the runs are already transparent (only non-transparent pixels are stored). For GPIC there's no transparency handling in PutSprite — it's a raw blit (used for backgrounds etc.). Tiles are drawn with TILE_Put which copies raw (tiles are GPIC type). Let me verify by reading GFX_DrawSprite... Actually GFX_PutSprite with rval=1 does `GFX_DrawSprite(dest, inmem)` which just memcpy? Let me check GFX_DrawSprite. Hmm — case 1 is when the sprite is fully on-screen; it calls GFX_DrawSprite which presumably copies each line. {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'thinking', 'thinking': 'The FX items are VOC files. I\'ll implement a VOC decoder in the extraction tool. VOC format:\n- Header "Creative Voice File" then 0x1A, then version/checksum.\n- Blocks: type byte, length 3 bytes little-endian (24-bit). For type 1 (sound data): rate byte, then data.\n\nThe Fx effects are in FILE0000.GLB. // KEYFILE.offset field == item count\n  const byIndex = [];\n  const byName = new Map();\n  for (let i = 0; i < numItems; i++) {\n    const off = 28 + i * 28;\n    const dec = decrypt(SERIAL, bytes.subarray(off, off + 28));\n    const kf = parseKeyfile(dec);\n    byIndex.push({ index: i, name: kf.name, opt: kf.opt, offset: kf.offset, filesize: kf.filesize });\n    if (!byName.has(kf.name)) byName.set(kf.name, []);\n    byName.get(kf.name).push(i);\n  }\n  return { bytes, count: numItems, byIndex, byName };\n}\n\n// Fetch item data by index.\nexport function getItemIndex(glb, index) {\n  const meta = glb.byIndex[index];\n  if (!meta) return null;\n  const raw = glb.bytes.subarray(meta.offset, meta.offset + meta.filesize);\n  if (meta.opt === 1) return decrypt(SERIAL, raw);\n  return raw;\n}\n\n// Fetch item data by unique name.\nexport function getItem(glb, name) {\n  const indices = glb.byName.get(name);\n  if (!indices || indices.length === 0) return null;\n  return getItemIndex(glb, indices[0]);\n}'}, 'partialArgs': '{"path": "D:/dev/ab-tasks/raptor-dsv4/tools/glb.mjs", "old_string": "// Opens a GLB file, returns { items: Map<name, {opt, offset, filesize}>, bytes }\\nexport function readGlb(buffer) {\\n  const bytes = new Uint8Array(buffer);\\n  const key = new Uint8Array(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, 28);\\n  const head = decrypt(SERIAL, key.slice());\\n  const numItems = u32(head, 4); DWORD offset; DWORD filesize; CHAR name[16]; }  == 28 bytes\n\nexport const SEED = 0x19; // 25\nconst SERIAL = "32768GLB";\n\n// GLB_DeCrypt from GLBAPI.C, byte-exact.\nexport function decrypt(keyStr, buf) {\n  const key = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < keyStr.length; i++) key.push(keyStr.charCodeAt(i));\n  const klen = key.length;\n  let kidx = SEED % klen;\n  let prev = key[kidx];\n  const out = new Uint8Array(buf.length);\n  for (let i = 0; i < buf.length; i++) {\n    const b = buf[i];\n    const d = (b - key[kidx] - prev) & 0xff;\n    prev = b;\n    out[i] = d;\n    if (++kidx >= klen) kidx = 0;\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport function u32(u8, o) {\n  return u8[o] | (u8[o + 1] << 8) | (u8[o + 2] << 16) | (u8[o + 3] << 24);\n}\nexport function u16(u8, o) {\n  return u8[o] | (u8[o + 1] << 8);\n}\nexport function i16(u8, o) {\n  const v = u8[o] | (u8[o + 1] << 8);\n  return v >= 0x8000 ? v - 0x10000 : v;\n}\nexport function i32(u8, o) {\n  return u32(u8, o) | 0;\n}\n\nexport function parseKeyfile(dec) {\n  return {\n    opt: u32(dec, 0),\n    offset: u32(dec, 4),\n    filesize: u32(dec, 8),\n    name: decToString(dec.subarray(12, 28)),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction decToString(u8) {\n  let s = "";\n  for (let i = 0; i < u8.length; i++) {\n    if (u8[i] === 0) break;\n    s += String.fromCharCode(u8[i]);\n  }\n  return s;\n}\n\n// Opens a GLB file, returns { items: Map<name, {opt, offset, filesize}>, bytes }\nexport function readGlb(buffer) {\n  const bytes = new Uint8Array(buffer);\n  const key = new Uint8Array(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, 28);\n  const head = decrypt(SERIAL, key.slice());\n  const numItems = u32(head, 4); // KEYFILE.offset field == item count\n  const items = new Map();\n  for (let i = 0; i < numItems; i++) {\n    const off = 28 + i * 28;\n    const dec = decrypt(SERIAL, bytes.subarray(off, off + 28));\n    const kf = parseKeyfile(dec);\n    items.set(kf.name, { opt: kf.opt, offset: kf.offset, filesize: kf.filesize });\n  }\n  return { bytes, items };\n}\n\nexport function getItem(glb, name) {\n  const meta = glb.items.get(name);\n  if (!meta) return null;\n  const raw = glb.bytes.subarray(meta.offset, meta.offset + meta.filesize);\n  if (meta.opt === 1) {\n    return decrypt(SERIAL, raw);\n  }\n  return raw;\n}\n', 'newText': '// GLB (Game Library) archive reader for the DOS Raptor shareware data files.\n// Reverse-engineered from SOURCE/../GFX/GLBAPI.C — Scott Host\'s GLB format.\n//\n// File layout (all multi-byte ints little-endian):\n//   [ KEYFILE ]            encrypted with serial "32768GLB"\n//   [ IDT: KEYFILE x N ]  each encrypted with the same serial\n//   item data blobs at KEYFILE.offset, each optionally encrypted (opt==GLB_ENCODED)\n//\n// KEYFILE { DWORD opt;
